Billionaire Lord’s Prestigious Italian Superyacht Is Asking for $27M
33 photos
Photo: TWW Yachts
“Andiamo” is a classy Italian name well-suited for an elegant superyacht built by one of the most prestigious shipyards in Italy. Although primarily known as the floating luxury toy of a billionaire English Lord, this yacht isn’t flashy and has managed to stayed away from media headlines and gossip; in fact, it could be simply described as pure balance.
One of the superyachts in the above-50-meter range that have recently joined the pre-loved yacht market doesn’t claim to be revolutionary or particularly striking. Its balanced look and overall qualities are what make it so appealing. You might even say that this isn’t the typical billionaire’s luxury toy, in the sense that there’s nothing sensational, outrageous, or immensely innovative about it. Still, it has all that it takes to be highly coveted.
Andiamo is not a new yacht, yet it had undergone a comprehensive refit recently enough to be considered “as good as new”. Most importantly, it carries the pedigree of one of the oldest and most reputable yacht builders in Europe, the famous Benetti, and that kind of heritage comes first even in comparison to a brand-new yacht in the same size, but from a lesser-known shipyard.
Andiamo was delivered in 2009 as Lady Lara. It is reported that it was originally built for a mining industry magnate from Kazakhstan, billionaire Alexander Machkevitch. The Italian yacht’s original name, Lady Lara, seems to have been inspired by the name of Machkevitch’s wife, Larissa. As we’ll see, Andiamo went from billionaire to billionaire, as one of the few “lucky” pleasure craft in this niche category to have only a couple of owners over decades.
Photo: TWW Yachts Usually, a superyacht that’s almost twenty-year-old would have a long list of former owners behind it, but that’s not the case with Andiamo. It changed hands once, going from Machkevitch to an unknown owner, and that’s when it was renamed Lady Luck. After that, it only changed hands again one more time, in 2017, when it was purchased by the one who is reportedly still its current owner after almost a decade – Sir Michael Hintze.
Lord Hintze was born in China to Russian parents, but was raised in Australia and eventually established himself in London, where the hedge-fund company he founded eventually made him a billionaire. He was knighted in 2013 for “services to the arts” (meaning hefty charitable contributions in this field) and later elevated to the House of Lords. Forbes currently ranks his fortune at $2.7 billion.
Almost a decade ago, when Lord Hintze allegedly purchased Lady Luck and renamed it Andiamo, the Italian yacht was listed at €35 million ($39 million today). Now, when the yacht has rejoined the market in search of a new owner, brokers claims that the current owner has spent more than €15 million ($16.7 million) in refits and upgrades over the years. That alone is an enormous sum, especially if you add it to the original selling price in 2017.
Still, it’s no secret that even the most luxurious yachts lose value relatively fast and that they cost their owners a lot of money in the end. Very few of these wealthy yacht owners, especially in the billionaire ranks, see these luxury toys as investments – they know they’ll pump more money into them than what they’re getting back (if anything), and it doesn’t stop them from buying an even more expensive yacht the next time.
Photo: TWW Yachts Andiamo’s most recent refit was completed relatively recently, in 2020, in Florida. The most striking and immediately recognizable change was its hull going from the standard white of many luxury yacht to a bold navy blue. The drastic paint job was part of a full exterior and interior revamping under the guidance of Patrick Knowles.
Refreshed and looking better than ever, this 17-year-old yacht has market appeal galore, starting with its undeniable Italian elegance. It combines a superyacht length of a little over 59 meters (195 feet) with 10.4-meter (34 feet) beam, a 3-meter (9.8 feet) draft, and a volume of just under 1000 GT (996 GT).
In short, this sums up as a yacht with considerable internal volume (perfect for comfortable accommodation) and access to smaller bays whether other yachts can’t reach, while the full-displacement hull design ensures greater stability for guests at anchor.
Andiamo’s elegant proportions and timeless style are owed to the original team that brought together Stefano Natucci for the exterior design, Benetti’s in-house team for naval architecture, and Studio Massari Interior Architecture and Design for the interior design, with all interior furnishings from the famous Italian Fendi brand. After the major 2020 refit, Andiamo’s interior and exterior carry the overlaying signature of Patrick Knowles.
Photo: TWW Yachts The generous six-stateroom layout can accommodate up to 12 guests, attended by a sizeable 15-person crew. The master suite takes center stage quite literally, spanning across two levels. This premium location makes room for a classic master’s office, a luxurious en-suite, and a modern observation lounge, in addition to the suite itself. Four guest cabins are located on the lower deck, while a VIP cabin and the Captain’s cabin are placed on the bridge deck.
Like any self-respecting luxury yacht, Andiamo pays great attention to outdoor living. The sun deck (everyone’s favorite place onboard) houses a large jacuzzi, plenty of sunbathing and lounging options, plus a contemporary-style outdoor gym. At water level, the transom turns into a spacious beach club with easy access to the water, as well as the garage that’s packed-full with water toys.
The new color palette clearly evokes a timeless maritime theme with bright blue and turquoise accents in conjunction with classic white – it matches the new hull paint color, and it makes Andiamo’s interior overall more visually striking. There’s also a bit of glam present, in the form of crystal, gold, and pearl accents, as well as high-quality marbles, woods, and lacquered finishes. Even the elevator that connects all decks is gold-plated for a more ornamental effect.
Performance-wise, Andiamo promises a cruising speed of 15 knots and a range of up to 6,000 nautical miles, powered by twin MTU engines. This means that Andiamo is just as good at transatlantic crossings as it is at accessing romantic little bays. Plus, recently-added zero-speed stabilizers ensure that the onboard experience is even more comfortable.
Photo: TWW Yachts It's also important to note that, although it has operated with great success on the luxury charter market in its past, Andiamo has taken a break from it over the past five years, during which it was enjoyed exclusively as a private pleasure craft. However, the yacht comes fully MLC-compliant and with low engine hours, which leaves it up to the next owner whether they will put this Italian beauty back on the charter market or not.
Andiamo’s current price tag is indicating €24 million ($26.9 million), which is not a lot, considering that it comes in great shape, fully refitted, and with overall investments valued at more than $15 million.
Above all, Andiamo comes from one of the most prestigious superyacht builders in Europe. Benetti has a long history spanning 150 years, and it’s the name behind several ultra-famous yachts, such as Spectre, Freedom, and Soundwave, all carrying the signature of iconic designers like Stefano Natucci and Giorgio Cassetta.
